notes: Hancock treats contemporary rock and R&B material as modern jazz repertoire rather than as novelty covers.
The core group includes Herbie Hancock, Michael Brecker, John Scofield, Dave Holland, Jack DeJohnette and Don Alias; selected tracks add strings and woodwinds/brass.
A solo-guitar album of songs written by others, and Metheny's first album without his own compositions.
The record uses several guitar configurations, including baritone, 42-string, 6-string and nylon-string guitars.

tracks.title: That's the Way I've Always Heard It Should Be

notes: A live solo-piano set built around ten Beatles songs, followed by David Bowie’s “Life on Mars?” as a bridge to later pop songwriting.
Recorded at Philharmonie de Paris in September 2020.
Ryan Adams re-recorded Taylor Swift’s 1989 song-for-song, shifting the material toward a looser singer-songwriter and rock palette.
The album was produced by Ryan Adams and Charlie Stavish.

tracks.title: All You Had to Do Was Stay

notes: Ten Bon Scott-era AC/DC songs are stripped down and substantially rearranged rather than reproduced as hard-rock covers.
The record is a useful example of how dramatically familiar material can change when arrangement and scale are reduced.

tracks.title: Up to My Neck in You
You Ain't Got a Hold on Me

notes: Hynde and James Walbourne assembled the Dylan set remotely during lockdown, building arrangements by sending ideas and recordings back and forth.
The nine-song collection stays focused on Dylan rather than mixing the tribute with unrelated material.

tracks.title: Don't Fall Apart on Me Tonight

notes: The first Lu’s Jukebox set is a Tom Petty tribute drawn from across his catalog and performed as a full-band studio concert.
The closing track, “Stolen Moments,” is a Lucinda Williams original rather than a Petty cover.

tracks.title: You Don't Know How It Feels

notes: The trio deliberately jumps across pop, country, electronic music and avant-garde jazz while keeping the instrumentation acoustic.
This is a useful CoverVerse stress test: nearly every track points to a different source artist.
Amos built the concept around songs written and originally performed by men, reframing each through a female character or point of view.
The source material ranges from hip-hop and metal to classic rock, synth-pop and singer-songwriter material.
Gabriel deliberately avoided a conventional rock-band treatment, rebuilding twelve favorite songs around voice and orchestral instrumentation.
The album was conceived as one half of a song-exchange project in which the source artists were invited to cover Gabriel songs in return.

tracks.title: I Think It's Going to Rain Today

notes: Frisell’s quintet treats Lennon material from both the Beatles catalog and Lennon’s solo years as a single songbook.
The arrangements are built around ensemble interplay rather than vocals, with guitar, violin, pedal steel/acoustic guitar, bass and drums.

tracks.title: You've Got to Hide Your Love Away

notes: Punch Brothers reimagined Tony Rice’s 1983 album Church Street Blues in sequence, treating Rice’s recording as the source album even though the songs themselves come from many writers and traditions.
The band described the project as both a standalone work and a gift to Rice.
Stardust is a ten-song collection of American pop standards, produced and arranged by Booker T. Jones.
These standards do not map cleanly to one source recording, so MusicVerse leaves original-artist fields unknown rather than treating a songwriter or a famous later interpreter as the original artist.

tracks.title: On the Sunny Side of the Street

originalArtists: Mae West with Duke Ellington's Orchestra
notes: Chan Marshall reduces a deliberately wide songbook to sparse voice, guitar and piano, often changing the emotional center of familiar material rather than reproducing the source arrangement.
Eleven tracks reinterpret other artists; “In This Hole” is a new version of Cat Power’s own song from What Would the Community Think.

tracks.title: Troubled Waters
tracks.originalArtist: Mae West with Duke Ellington's Orchestra

notes: Sam Beam and Ben Bridwell treat the record as a shared songbook rather than a tribute to one artist, moving between new wave, soul, folk, country and psychedelic rock.
The performances are deliberately warm and understated, with the arrangements reshaped around the two singers and an acoustic-leaning multi-instrumental ensemble.

tracks.title: You Know More Than I Know
God Knows (You Gotta Give To Get)

notes: Hancock treats Joni Mitchell's writing as jazz repertoire rather than as a straight tribute, using elastic arrangements and a core quintet built around Wayne Shorter, Lionel Loueke, Dave Holland and Vinnie Colaiuta.
Eight of the ten tracks are Mitchell compositions. Duke Ellington's “Solitude” and Wayne Shorter's “Nefertiti” were included because of their importance to Mitchell's musical development.
Guest voices are used selectively: Norah Jones, Tina Turner, Corinne Bailey Rae, Joni Mitchell, Luciana Souza and Leonard Cohen.

tracks.title: The Tea Leaf Prophecy (Lay Down Your Arms)

notes: Welch and Rawlings recorded this ten-song acoustic covers set at home, stripping the material down to two voices and two guitars.

The repertoire moves between traditional songs and writers including Elizabeth Cotten, Bob Dylan, John Prine and Norman Blake; “Jackson,” written by Billy Edd Wheeler and Jerry Leiber, became especially well known through Johnny Cash and June Carter.
The album was originally issued in July 2020 and later won the Grammy Award for Best Folk Album.

tracks.title: Oh Babe It Ain't No Lie
Fly Around My Pretty Little Miss
All The Good Times Are Past And Gone

notes: Tedeschi Trucks Band performed Derek and the Dominos' Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs in sequence at LOCKN' on August 24, 2019, with Trey Anastasio and Doyle Bramhall II joining the ensemble.
The album preserves the full live performance and adds a studio duet of “Thorn Tree in the Garden” by Derek Trucks and Susan Tedeschi.

Because this project is explicitly a full-album revisit, MusicVerse treats Derek and the Dominos as the source artist for the track-level relationships, even where the 1970 Layla album itself drew on older blues material.

notes: Frisell treats American repertoire as one connected landscape, moving from Copland and Ives through blues, jazz, folk, pop and singer-songwriter material without changing the basic quintet.

The first seven tracks form a sequence from Aaron Copland's Billy the Kid. Two excerpts from Charles Ives' The "Saint-Gaudens" in Boston Common frame the album's central run of popular-song reinterpretations.
Nonesuch credits the album to Bill Frisell with Don Byron, Guy Klucevsek, Kermit Driscoll and Joey Baron, produced by Wayne Horvitz and recorded in March 1992.

notes: For All I Care is The Bad Plus's first album built entirely from other composers' music and its first to use a featured vocalist, Minneapolis singer Wendy Lewis.

The repertoire deliberately erases the usual wall between rock, pop, country and modern classical music, placing Nirvana, Pink Floyd, Wilco, Heart and the Bee Gees beside Ligeti, Babbitt and Stravinsky.
The album first appeared in Europe in October 2008; the U.S. Heads Up release followed on February 3, 2009.
Springsteen built the project around traditional and folk repertoire associated with Pete Seeger, recording the core album live in informal sessions rather than treating the songs as museum pieces.

MusicVerse follows the Spotify target already attached to this catalog record: the 18-track American Land Edition. It expands the original 13-track April 2006 album with five additional recordings and live performances.
The American Land Edition was released October 3, 2006. “American Land” is a Springsteen composition inspired by an immigrant-worker poem and is marked here as an original rather than a cover.

How Can a Poor Man Stand Such Times and Live

originalArtists: Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds
notes: Cat Power's second covers-centered album uses a full band and a Memphis-soul-informed palette rather than the stark reductions of The Covers Record.

The set ranges from country, blues and soul to Dylan, Joni Mitchell and Nick Cave. “Metal Heart” is a new recording of Cat Power's own earlier song, while “Song To Bobby” is an original written for this album.
Matador's standard digital configuration contains 13 tracks; other physical and deluxe editions vary in their bonus material.

tracks.title: Breathless
tracks.originalArtist: Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds

notes: Thompson built the project after being asked for a millennium-spanning best-songs list and took the premise literally, moving from medieval material to contemporary pop.
The live set is deliberately chronological and interpretive, with Thompson, Judith Owen and Michael Jerome stripping wildly different eras down to voice, guitar and percussion.

notes: The centerpiece is Phish's 1996 Halloween 'musical costume': a complete live performance of Talking Heads' Remain in Light as the second set.
The release preserves the full three-set concert and encore, so MusicVerse marks Phish originals separately from the Talking Heads set and the other covers.

tracks.title: Born Under Punches (The Heat Goes On)

notes: Hunter reworks Bob Marley & The Wailers' Natty Dread track-for-track as instrumental jazz rather than trying to reproduce the reggae arrangements.
The quartet's two-saxophone front line and Hunter's 8-string guitar turn the songs into a mix of soul-jazz, post-bop, funk and straight-ahead improvisation.
Scofield treats Ray Charles' repertoire as material for a jazz-and-R&B band rather than as a museum-piece tribute.

The record mixes instrumental arrangements with guest vocal turns from Dr. John, Warren Haynes, John Mayer, Mavis Staples and Aaron Neville, while longtime Ray Charles saxophonist David 'Fathead' Newman also appears.
